script: In the summer of 1942, Stalin signed an order so brutal that Soviet soldiers feared it more than the Germans. The Nazis were racing toward the oil fields of the Caucasus, and the Red Army kept falling back. So on July 28, Stalin issued Order Number 227, and its message was four words long: not one step back. Any soldier who retreated without orders would be treated as a traitor to the motherland. Blocking detachments took position behind the front lines, with orders to shoot their own retreating men. Deserters were thrown into penal battalions and handed the most suicidal missions of the entire war. But here is the part nobody agrees on, some historians say the order actually worked. Panic retreats slowed, the line at Stalingrad held, and the war began to turn. Others say it worked for a darker reason, soldiers simply learned that going back was more deadly than going forward. Stalin never apologized for Order 227, because for him fear was not a side effect, it was the strategy, and his own soldiers feared him to the very end.
